question: Does warm-start chaining, or a bigger budget, or neither, let this model carry the KV 0.070 spastic lesion it currently cannot?

chain_parent.why: the immediately milder rung of the same KV ladder, same seed, same min_velocity 1.0, same base model -- Ong et al.'s chaining is rung to rung, not arbitrary donor to recipient

init_syntax: init { file = "par/<name>.par" }  (relative to the config dir; SCONE is invoked with cwd = that dir)

init_settings.std_factor: NOT SET in any arm (SCONE default)
init_settings.std_offset: NOT SET in any arm (SCONE default)
init_settings.use_best_as_mean: NOT SET in any arm (SCONE default)
init_settings.why: the corpus sets none of them; setting any of them in arm B alone would confound chaining with a change of search width, which is the whole point of the probe

init_std_audit.interpretation: ratios near 1 mean arm B's search is not narrower than arm A's, so any difference in outcome is chaining, not search width

verdict.statement: WARM-START CHAINING IS THE FIX; COMPUTE IS NOT. Arm A reproduced the failure exactly (t_end 8.24 s, identical .par filenames to R291KV0070_s101). Arm B, which differs from A in exactly one config line -- the init file pointing at the optimised KV 0.050 solution instead of the unlesioned base -- reached t_end 13.95 s, clearing the 9.73 s gate and landing inside the 13.58-17.85 s analysis band, at a terminal objective of 37.23 against A's 64.24. Arm C, 3.7x the generations with no chaining, reached only t_end 9.23 s and objective 60.26, still below the gate, and stopped on its own convergence criterion. The corpus was asking a healthy controller to jump straight into a severe lesion; the controller cannot make that jump, but it can walk the lesion down a ladder. This is a PIPELINE defect in our launchers, not a limit of the model.
verdict.cost_of_the_fix: Chaining costs nothing extra in generations: arm B ran the same 90 generations as arm A. It costs 2.0x the wall clock (249.6 s vs 122.5 s) only because a controller that walks longer simulates longer. Arm C's failed compute path cost 4.0x arm A for no benefit.
verdict.single_seed_caveat: n = 1 seed, one condition. B clears the gate by 4.2 s, which is a large margin, but confirming the fix needs the remaining five seeds and at least one deeper rung.

reference_failure_all_six_seeds.note: gate is 9.73 s; all six fall short

arm_A_reproduction_check.meaning: arm A is a bit-for-bit reproduction of the corpus cell, not merely a similar run. The failure is fully reproducible, so every comparison below is against a solid baseline.

arm_C_early_stop.why: SCONE stopped on the config's own convergence rule, min_progress = 1e-4 over min_progress_samples = 200, which is inherited unchanged from the corpus config. C was therefore not truncated by us: the optimiser declared itself converged after 3.7x arm A's budget and it was still 0.50 s short of the gate. Reading C as 'we did not give it enough compute' is not supported -- it gave up on its own.
